source: 202526 Netball Coaches Manual, Passing, pages 79 to 83, Niel du Plessis and Erin Burger. The manual names this pass 'Double hand chest' and lists it FIRST under Passes in two practice plans, above 'Double hand over head' and '1 Hand wide'. A drill on manual page 86 opens with it: 'Player will start in front with ball passing chest pass to first player'. THE MANUAL GIVES IT NO TECHNIQUE BLOCK. Every other technique in this library quotes a numbered step from its own drill block. This one cannot, because no such block exists. Its cues are TRANSFERRED from the manual's other pass blocks, and each checkpoint names the block its cue came from. The numeric bands are NOT the manual's. They are PROVISIONAL and a coach must set them.
cueSourceNote: The manual's pass section gives numbered steps for OVERHEAD PASS, 1 HAND HIGH PASS, 1 HAND LOW WIDE PASS, 1 HAND WIDE PASS, 1/2 HAND BOUNCE PASS, UNDERARM PASS, LOB PASS (BOMB) and FAKE PASS. It gives none for the chest pass. Three instructions repeat across those blocks and are mechanics of any pass rather than of one pass: give a small step, do not give a too big step, and use the momentum rather than waiting. Those transfer. The biggest transfer in this file is the OVERHEAD block's warning, which reads IN FULL 'Keep hands where they were with catch, don't pull ball back behind head (waste time, change angle of release)'. IT IS QUOTED HERE WITH A DELIBERATE ELISION, marked: 'behind head' is dropped, because a chest pass has no behind-head position and the words that transfer are 'keep hands where they were' and 'don't pull ball back'. The parenthesis is kept as the REASON and not as a cue, because neither wasted time nor release angle has an instrument. Read the remainder as the chest pass's central coaching point. A coach must confirm that reading. It is a judgment, not a quotation. IT CARRIES NO CHECKPOINT: the motion keys hold the ball still at the step, so the movement obeys the cue, but no measure this engine has can tell whether an athlete obeyed it. Refer to pullBackMeasureNote.
releaseAnchorNote: The release phase is anchored AT the release, and the follow-through is graded as its own phase. This is deliberate and it is new. The four releasing drills already in the library anchor their release-named phase at phase 1.00 while the ball actually leaves at 0.805 to 0.953, so they grade the follow-through and call it the release. Measured on ac240b2: all four read within their own band at the frame their solved ballState turns to 'released', and below it at the frame they are graded on. One phase cannot be both the release and the follow-through, so here it is two.
stepMeasureNote: THE MANUAL'S OWN STEP CUE IS NOT GRADEABLE AND THIS FILE DOES NOT PRETEND IT IS. 'Give a small step' and 'don't give a too big step (shortening own 3ft)' are about step LENGTH. No measure in this engine reports step length: the foot measures are leftFootHeightCm, rightFootHeightCm and footHeightGapCm, all heights. The step phase therefore grades the weight transfer, which is what can be measured, and the length goes ungraded. The missing instrument is a foot separation measure. Naming it here rather than letting a green checkpoint imply the cue is covered.
pullBackMeasureNote: THE PULL-BACK IS ALSO NOT GRADEABLE, AND A CHECKPOINT FOR IT WAS AUTHORED HERE AND THEN REMOVED. The first draft graded leftElbowFlexionDegrees at the step phase, on the reasoning that a pull-back changes the arm. IT DOES NOT CHANGE IT ENOUGH TO SEE. Mutation test, identical on ed00825 and on ac240b2: moving the step key from the chest to the shoulder, across 0.22 to 0.20, up 0.05 to 0.20 and ahead 0.38 to 0.18, which is 13.2 cm on the reference athlete and more than half a netball's diameter, moved every measure this engine has by: elbow flexion 5.1 degrees, shoulder elevation 2.0, knee 0.4, trunk lean 0.4, trunk turn 0.0. The largest response is 5.1, which is the threshold this repository calls meaningless. The checkpoint passed the mutation, so it was not a check, and it was deleted rather than kept green. The missing instrument is a LINEAR measure of how far the ball sits ahead of the chest. Both missing instruments are distances, and this engine grades angles. That is the pattern, stated once here: two of this pass's three manual cues are distances.
trunkLeanNote: TRUNK LEAN DOES NOT RESPOND TO WHAT THIS DRILL AUTHORS, so this file grades no trunk lean. Sweeping the drive key over six positions, every reachable one, and hip drops from 0.11 to 0.35, the lean at the drive phase moved between 1.19 and 2.37 degrees and the whole-clip maximum never left 2.37. A LIBRARY-WIDE READING, offered to the movement lane rather than acted on here: seven trunk lean checkpoints exist across the other eight drills, and ALL SEVEN sit 8.87 to 19.76 degrees below their own ceiling, with each clip's maximum lean barely above the value graded. Measured on ac240b2. RE-MEASURED, AND THE FIRST READING IS SUPERSEDED: on ed00825 this note said only Hooks, Outside Hand came near its ceiling, at 12.05 against 16. PR #46, the hand mirror fix, moved that drill's lean to 6.96 with a whole-clip maximum of 7.13, so its headroom went from 3.95 to 8.87 and the one counterexample is gone. The reading is that lean follows the trunk turn, which the possession model drives, and not the hand keys or the hip drop. A drill that does not turn cannot fail a lean band. NOT PROVEN IN GENERAL, measured in one sweep on one drill plus the library's own numbers on two builds. ONE ANCHOR DISCREPANCY FOUND WHILE CHECKING THIS, and it is not in this file: netball_two_hand_catch_chest grades its pull_in phase at 0.72 while its own motion key named pull_in sits at 0.76, four frames apart on 98. Every other trunk lean checkpoint in the library sits exactly on the key of its own name. THE MEASURED EFFECT IS BELOW THE THRESHOLD: over those four frames the lean moves 0.02 degrees and the elbow 1.47, so no verdict changes and the 105 to 150 band this file borrows from that phase contains both readings, 144.39 and 145.86. Reported to the movement lane, not acted on here.
separationInstrumentNote: A WARNING ABOUT THE SEPARATION CHECK, found by the mutation above. movement_definition.separation() takes the MAXIMUM movement across a phase's checkpoints, so one checkpoint that moves well hides any number that do not. In the first draft this phase reported 10.77 degrees of separation on the knee while its elbow checkpoint moved 1.5 and was blind to the fault it named. phaseSeparation would have called the phase distinguishable and the receipt would have read 9 of 9. The mutation found it and the separation check could not have.

checkpoints.cue: Ball at your chest in two hands, fingers up and thumbs behind the middle of the ball.
checkpoints.why: TRANSFERRED from the manual's OVERHEAD PASS block, which opens 'Player catch the ball the same every time with 2 hands and fingers up and thumbs behind in the middle of the ball'. That sentence describes how a player holds the ball before ANY pass, so it applies here. BAND PROVISIONAL: taken from netball_two_hand_catch_chest's pull_in band, 105 to 150, because a chest pass starts in the pose a chest catch finishes in. The upper bound is anatomy rather than technique and the range of motion check already guards it.

checkpoints.cue: Balanced base, ready to pass straight away.
checkpoints.why: TRANSFERRED from the manual's repeated instruction to use the momentum and not wait: '1 HAND HIGH PASS' warns 'Don't wait too long to release', and the 2 HANDS CATCH block says 'Use momentum of catch to pass ball back as soon as possible'. A pass that leaves straight away needs a base already under it. BAND PROVISIONAL: the ready knee band used by the catch drills.

phases.name: step

checkpoints.cue: Give a small step. Do not step so big that you shorten your own three feet.
checkpoints.why: TRANSFERRED, and this cue is close to a quotation. ATTRIBUTION CORRECTED, because the blocks do NOT share one wording: 'Give a small step, and with wrist and hands pass the ball to other player' is the OVERHEAD block ALONE. 1 HAND LOW WIDE and 1 HAND WIDE both end 'pass the ball to other', 1 HAND HIGH ends 'pass the ball' with no recipient, and 1/2 HAND BOUNCE ends 'pass the ball to another player/wall'. WHAT ACTUALLY TRANSFERS is the opening five words, 'Give a small step, and', which all five blocks share verbatim; the recipient differs per block and is not carried into this cue. 'Don't give a too big step (shortening own 3ft)' appears in the OVERHEAD and 1 HAND HIGH blocks. WHAT THIS CHECKPOINT ACTUALLY GRADES IS THE WEIGHT TRANSFER, NOT THE STEP LENGTH, because step length has no measure. Refer to stepMeasureNote. BAND PROVISIONAL and authored from coaching intent rather than from a solve: below 35 she has not loaded the step at all, above 85 she has dropped into a lunge and lost the quick release.

phases.removedCheckpointNote: A second checkpoint here graded leftElbowFlexionDegrees against the manual's 'Keep hands where they were with catch, don't pull ball back behind head', quoted in the cue with 'behind head' elided; refer to cueSourceNote. It was REMOVED because a mutation proved it cannot fail. Refer to pullBackMeasureNote. The cue is still the biggest transfer this file makes and it still needs a coach's ruling, but it needs an instrument first, so it is recorded as a gap rather than as a green checkpoint.

phases.name: drive

checkpoints.cue: Pass with your wrists and hands. Do not push the ball with your arm.
checkpoints.why: TRANSFERRED from the 1 HAND HIGH PASS block's warning 'Don't push the ball with arm', and from the wording shared by three blocks, 'with wrist and hands pass the ball'. BAND PROVISIONAL: the ball has left the chest and the arm is extending but is not straight. The lower bound guards an arm already locked out this early, which is the push the manual warns against.

phases.removedCheckpointNote: A trunkLeanDegrees checkpoint at 0 to 14 was authored here, cueing 'Do not throw your chest after the ball', and REMOVED for the same reason as the step's second checkpoint: a mutation could not make it fail. Sweeping the drive key over every reachable hand position and hip drop moved the trunk lean between 1.19 and 2.37 degrees, against a ceiling of 14. Refer to trunkLeanNote.

checkpoints.cue: Let it go early. Use the momentum, do not wait.
checkpoints.why: TRANSFERRED from '1 HAND HIGH PASS': 'Don't wait too long to release, use momentum pull wide and release', and from '1 HAND LOW WIDE PASS': 'Use momentum, pull wide back and release'. BAND PROVISIONAL, and it is the best evidenced band in this file. The three releasing catch drills band this same measure at 55 to 115, 45 to 105 and 50 to 120, and measured on ac240b2 the elbow at the frame their ballState turns to 'released' is 98.0, 86.8, 99.3 and 98.7. 55 to 115 is the tightest of the three analogue bands and it contains all four measurements. IT INHERITS AN OPEN QUESTION: those same three bands are currently recorded as failing, because they are read at phase 1.00 rather than at the release. Refer to releaseAnchorNote. If the coach morning moves those anchors, this band is confirmed. If it widens those bands instead, this band must be revisited.

checkpoints.cue: Finish with your fingers pointing after the ball.
checkpoints.why: AUTHORED from the engine's own behaviour and flagged as such. No manual sentence describes a chest pass follow-through. This phase exists because the release phase above must grade the release and not the frames after it, and the extension after the ball has gone is a real thing a coach can see. BAND PROVISIONAL: measured on ac240b2, the four releasing drills read 40.9, 40.9, 50.0 and 35.8 at their last frame, and 25 to 70 contains all four with margin. A coach may decide she does not grade a follow-through at all, in which case this phase goes.
